## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Ambavimānavatthu* ("Mango Mansion") is the forty-sixth discourse in the *Vimānavatthu*, a collection preserved in the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. The narrative centers on the karmic fruition of generosity, depicting the spiritual and heavenly rewards that result from offering a monastery to the Saṅgha or monastic order [SuttaCentral].
The text is preserved with its traditional commentary in the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, which shares extensive passages with the canonical verses (§1.1–10.2) [DharmaNexus]. Text-reuse analysis conducted by DharmaNexus indicates substantial internal reuse with formulaic verse segments across the *Vimānavatthu*, showing extensive shared passages with texts such as the *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), the *Caturitthivimānavatthu* (Vv 45), the *Dutiyasūcivimānavatthu* (Vv 59), and the *Maṇithūṇavimānavatthu* (Vv 77) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records low-scoring automatic alignments with the Tibetan translation of the *Saddharmasmṛtyupasthānasūtra* (*’phags pa dam pa’i chos dran pa nye bar gzhag pa*, D0287-2) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
